notes: PSA 3.8 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.13. Prostate volume 30 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.79.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prior prostate cancer diagnosis to discuss treatment options.

Recently retired harbour pilot (semi-retired) with a history of lower abdominal surgery. The patient reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, IPSS score 8/35. He is married but lives alone, with his spouse as the primary next-of-kin. He exercises regularly, running 3 times a week for 5 km, and consumes approximately 6 units of alcohol weekly. He is an ex-smoker, having quit in 2018 after 13 pack-years. He attends a pain clinic for chronic shoulder pain. No active medications or known allergies. PSA trend shows a significant rise from 1.1 ng/mL in November 2023 to 3.8 ng/mL in February 2025.

On DRE, a nodule is palpable in the right lobe, consistent with clinical T stage cT2. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vitals, BP 146/78 mmHg, HR 80 bpm. No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly detected.
